test_title: SSC MTS 2025 Official Paper (Held On: 09 Feb, 2026 Shift 3)
subject: general
question:
Which of the following options is the most suitable conversion of the following sentence into Passive Voice?

Will the committee approve the new policy tomorrow?

options.text: Has the new policy been approved by the committee tomorrow?
Will the new policy be approved by the committee tomorrow?
Will the new policy be approving by the committee tomorrow?
Was the new policy approved by the committee tomorrow?

solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Will the new policy be approved by the committee tomorrow?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in the **future tense** and is in active voice.
 
• The sentence asks about an action (approval of the new policy) that will take place in the future.
 
• When converting a sentence into passive voice, the object of the active sentence becomes the subject of the passive sentence.
 
• In the passive voice, the structure for future tense is **Will + be + past participle**.

Correct conversion: *Will the new policy be approved by the committee tomorrow?*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Active Voice:** The subject performs the action. Example: The committee will approve the new policy.
 
• **Passive Voice:** The subject receives the action. Example: The new policy will be approved by the committee.
 
• **Incorrect Options:**
 
 
• **Option 1:** "Has the new policy been approved by the committee tomorrow?" is incorrect because "has been approved" indicates present perfect tense, which does not align with "tomorrow" (future time).
 
• **Option 3:** "Will the new policy be approving by the committee tomorrow?" is incorrect because "be approving" is grammatically incorrect in this context.
 
• **Option 4:** "Was the new policy approved by the committee tomorrow?" is incorrect because "was approved" indicates past tense, which does not align with "tomorrow" (future time).
